name: Vosual - AI音声認識 文字起こし
oneLine: A free Japanese iPhone and iPad app from BarrierBreak that turns speech into text with one button, made to replace written notes (筆談) with people who are hard of hearing.

platforms.detail: Vosual is an iPhone and iPad app. The App Store also lets it run on Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision Pro as an iPad app, noting it is not verified for macOS. Its website lists iPhone only, and a Google Play search finds no Vosual app.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 12.0 or later for iPhone and iPadOS 12.0 or later for iPad. The website lists iPhone on iOS 12 to iOS 18 and iOS 26. Use without internet needs a device with an A12 Bionic chip or newer.

roomCaptions.text: Yes, tap one button and speak
roomCaptions.detail: Speech picked up by the microphone is turned into text on screen. You start it with a single button (話しかける, "speak"), so children and older people can use it; a setting decides whether voice input ends by itself.

groupConversations.detail: Vosual presents itself as a replacement for written notes between two people. Group conversations are not described.

languages.detail: The website lists Japanese as the supported language and says more languages are planned. The app's own menus are in Japanese and English.

offline.text: Partly: iPhones with an A12 chip or newer
offline.detail: The website says Wi-Fi or mobile data is required. The terms say devices with an A12 Bionic chip or newer can also recognise speech offline, possibly less accurately, for people who don't want audio sent to a server.

speakerLabels.detail: Vosual's pages don't describe telling speakers apart.

voiceNames.detail: Recognising people by their voice is not described.

speakerDirection.detail: Showing where a voice comes from is not described.

translation.detail: Vosual's pages describe Japanese speech to Japanese text; translation is not described.

saveTranscripts.detail: Saving conversations is not described. The terms say Vosual itself does not collect, store or reuse audio or the converted text.

export.detail: Sharing or exporting text is not described.

fileUpload.detail: Vosual's pages describe live speech from the microphone, not transcribing audio or video files.

customWords.detail: A word list is not described. A text correction feature lets you fix words on screen.

display.text: Text zoom; text area turns around
display.detail: Updates added enlarging and shrinking the text, correcting text by hand, and turning the text area around (so the person opposite can read it). Colour or contrast options are not described.

soundAlerts.detail: Alerts for sounds like a doorbell or an alarm are not described.

phoneCalls.detail: Captioning phone calls is not described.

videoCalls.detail: Captioning video calls is not described.

mediaOnDevice.detail: Captioning audio playing on the phone is not described.

humanCaptioners.detail: The terms say the text comes from Apple's speech recognition engine. No human captioners are described.

signLanguage.detail: Vosual turns speech into text. Its website recommends it to people looking for a way to communicate other than sign language or written notes.

privacy.text: Apple's servers; offline on A12 or newer
privacy.detail: The terms say audio is sent to Apple's servers to become text and Apple may use it to improve its engine; Vosual itself does not collect, store or reuse audio or text. On A12 Bionic or newer devices it can work offline. The app shows Google AdMob ads, and its App Store privacy label lists identifiers, usage data and diagnostics that may be used to track you.

account.detail: No sign-up is described. The privacy policy says the only personal information it handles is what you enter when you contact the developer.

availability.detail: Listed on the Japanese App Store since November 2017. Apple's store data did not find it in the US, UK, Korean, Taiwanese, Australian or German stores (November 2026). Not on Google Play.

freePlan.detail: Free to download, with no in-app purchases on the Japanese App Store (November 2026). The listing says it contains ads, and the privacy policy names Google AdMob. Usage limits are not described.

price.detail: The Japanese App Store lists the app as free with no in-app purchases (November 2026).

accessibilityFunding.detail: No funding programme is described; the app is free. Its website points businesses to Japan's duty, since 1 April 2024, to provide reasonable accommodation to people with disabilities, and offers Vosual as one way to do that.

strengths.text: One button starts the conversation, so children and older people can use it as a replacement for written notes.
It is free, with no in-app purchases on the Japanese App Store.
It runs on iPhones and iPads with iOS 12 or later, and offline on devices with an A12 Bionic chip or newer.
The text can be enlarged, corrected by hand and turned around for the person opposite.

limits.text: It captions Japanese only and runs only on Apple devices; there is no Android app.
The website says Wi-Fi or mobile data is required; offline use needs an A12 Bionic chip or newer.
It shows Google AdMob ads, and its privacy label lists data that may be used to track you.
Its pages don't describe saving, sharing or translating conversations.

sources.title: ご利用規約 (Vosual terms of use)
sources.label: Vosual terms of use
quotes: 本アプリの音声認識機能は、Apple社の音声認識エンジンを利用して音声データをテキストに変換し、画面上に表示するためのものとなります。
本アプリでは、音声データおよび変換後のテキストデータを収集・保存・分析・再利用などに使用することは一切ありません。
ただし、Apple社の音声認識エンジンを利用している関係上、音声データはApple社のサーバーに送信され、テキスト変換処理が行われます。そのため、Apple社においては音声認識エンジンの学習や精度向上などに活用される可能性があることはご理解ください。
なお、A12 Bionic以降のチップを搭載したiOSデバイスでは、オフライン環境でも音声認識の利用が可能です。サーバーへの音声データ送信を避けたい場合は、認識精度が低下する可能性はありますが、オフラインでのご利用もご検討ください。

notes: The seller URL on the App Store (http://www.barrierbreak.jp/vosual/) is a one-line page that forwards to https://barrierbreak.sakura.ne.jp/vosual/jp/, which is used here. All pages were opened on 2026-11-02 with curl (website, terms, privacy policy, contact page, Japanese App Store page, lookup API). Conflicts: (1) Offline: the website says 'Wi-Fiまたはモバイル通信必須' (Wi-Fi or mobile data required), while the terms (in force since 1 November 2017, with A12 wording added later) and the 2.5.2 update note say devices with an A12 Bionic chip or newer can recognise speech offline; the table shows 'partly'. (2) Platforms: the website lists iPhone only; the App Store lists iPhone, iPad and iPod touch, plus Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision as an iPad app 'not verified for macOS'. (3) Sign language: the website says 'for people looking for a communication tool other than sign language and written notes', the App Store description says only 'other than written notes'. Ads: the listing's information section says it contains ads, the privacy policy names Google AdMob, and the privacy label lists identifiers, usage data and diagnostics used for tracking and third-party advertising. Not found on any page: saving or sharing conversations, translation, speaker labels, file transcription, colour options, usage limits, the developer's city. Android: a Google Play search for 'ボジュアル' returns no results, and a search for 'Vosual' (Japan) lists only unrelated apps; the website names iPhone only. The App Store lookup returned the app for Japan only (US, UK, Korea, Taiwan, Australia and Germany checked). A review on the listing asks for an Android version; reviews are not used on the page. Caption accuracy was not checked.
